bullets.title: AMD Q2 beats but -8% post-earnings on capex shock
bullets.body: AMD reported Q2 revenue of $11.54B (+50% YoY) with Data Center doubling to $6.72B and non-GAAP EPS of $1.66 vs. $1.62 estimate—all beats. Stock fell ~8% on Q2 capex of $808M vs. $298.6M expected, nearly triple consensus. Q3 guidance of $12.70–$13.30B (midpoint $13B) topped the $12.51B consensus, but fintwit reads the capex surprise as a signal the market punished a stock priced for perfection. One account notes AMD's capex positions it for 2026–27 outgrowth, arguing the selloff is an overreaction.

bullets.title: SpaceX commits to NVDA-exclusive GPU supply; satellite AI compute confirmed
bullets.body: On its first public earnings call, SpaceX CEO Musk confirmed the company is building exclusively on NVIDIA chips going forward and expects a 'significant percentage' of NVIDIA GPU output next year. The Starmind AI1 satellite compute payload will use NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 GPUs and Vera CPUs. SpaceX reported Q2 revenue of $7.8B (+92% YoY), adj. EBITDA $3.5B (+191% YoY), AI segment revenue $2.56B, and $100B in cash/securities, yet shares fell ~7% post-market on share lockup concerns ahead of a 136.95M share secondary.

bullets.title: COHR, AAOI, LITE, FN flagged as primary optical beneficiaries of China transceiver curbs
bullets.body: Sell-side consensus identifies COHR and AAOI as main beneficiaries of FCC restrictions on Chinese data-center optical transceivers, with FN and LITE as secondary plays. COHR separately secured a CHIPS Act LOI for up to $50M to quadruple InP wafer capacity at its Sherman, Texas facility. Counterpoint Research warns that missing a single batch of Chinese transceivers can idle billion-dollar GPU allocations, amplifying the supply-chain urgency for domestic alternatives.

bullets.title: MU: HBM demand sold out through 2027; CXL broadening inference memory spend
bullets.body: Digitimes reports SK Hynix, Micron, and Samsung have fully allocated 2027 DRAM and HBM production capacity. Separately, CXL momentum is described as confirming memory capacity and pricing stress while broadening inference memory spend beyond HBM—a positive, high-magnitude catalyst for Micron. One account summarizes: 'AJ and Micron = no brainer.'

bullets.title: ANET Q2: AI networking demand 'vastly outpaces supply'; growth broadening beyond back-end
bullets.body: Arista Networks Q2 2026 earnings call read-throughs indicate AI networking demand materially exceeds available supply, with growth expanding beyond back-end data center infrastructure across a broader customer base. Operating margin came in at 48.8% vs. 46.8% consensus. Liquid cooling adoption is flagged as expanding from accelerators into the broader network fabric, benefiting ANET alongside COHR and LITE.

bullets.title: ALAB Q2 strong beat; AI infra spending broadening into switching and signal conditioning
bullets.body: Astera Labs reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.83 vs. $0.69 estimate and revenue of $392M vs. $360M estimate—a ~20% and ~9% beat respectively. Earnings call read-throughs show AI infrastructure spending broadening beyond accelerator silicon into high-radix scale-up switching and signal conditioning. NBIS, AAOI, and ALAB each surged 33–50% in the five trading days surrounding earnings.

bullets.title: PLTR surges 25%+ on 'otherworldly' commercial demand; HSBC raises PT to $162
bullets.body: Palantir soared after boosting forecasts and describing commercial demand as 'otherworldly.' HSBC raised its price target from $151 to $162. Michael Burry remains short PLTR (closed Jan 2026 puts but rolled the short). A separate report notes Palantir is shifting European profits to the U.S. to minimize European tax liability.

bullets.title: GOOGL commits $150B to AI chip infrastructure; Gemini expands to all ages in Classroom
bullets.body: Google's reported $150B commitment to AI chip infrastructure signals intensifying competition in AI compute capacity with potential to influence semiconductor and networking pricing dynamics. Separately, Google is expanding Gemini AI to all ages in Google Classroom starting August 10, with K-12 rollout underway.

bullets.title: TSEM: Tower Semi raises 2028 model by $800M; silicon wafer supply tightening
bullets.body: Tower Semiconductor lifted its 2028 revenue forecast by $800M following Q2 2026 earnings that showed AI spending broadening into optical interconnects and analog power. Separately, GlobalWafers reports 12-inch, 8-inch, and 6-inch silicon wafer capacity is nearly full with demand recovering, with meaningful 2027 revenue growth expected from new capacity.

bullets.title: MRVL: Memory access—not compute—is the AI inference bottleneck; CXL positioning strong
bullets.body: Marvell highlighted that GPU utilization in AI inference is increasingly constrained by memory access as KV caches grow, not compute capacity. Flash Memory Summit attendees note Marvell's Celestial platform is well-positioned for the CXL opportunity.

bullets.title: MSFT: 605 Redmond layoffs filed; $637M dark pool print signals post-earnings selling
bullets.body: Microsoft filed a WARN notice for 605 workers in Redmond effective September 4, 2026. Separately, a $637M dark pool print in MSFT was flagged post-earnings rally, suggesting a large shareholder cashing out. Burry disclosed he exited his MSFT long calls entirely.

bullets.title: BKNG Q2 beats across all metrics; guides Q3 +5-7% at constant FX
bullets.body: Booking Holdings posted Q2 revenue of $7.35B (est. $7.18B), gross bookings $51.0B (est. $49.68B), and adj. EBITDA $2.65B (est. $2.56B). Q3 revenue guidance of +5–7% at constant FX and room night growth of +3–5%. CEO cited resilient U.S. demand (high single digits) and Middle East conflict as a headwind to long-haul travel, while AI-driven referrals remain a small but growing contributor.

bullets.title: AAPL faces DRAM cost pressure as CXMT rejects price-cut request
bullets.body: South Korean media reports Apple recently negotiated with China's CXMT for lower LPDDR5X DRAM prices ahead of next-gen iPhone production—and was rejected. This strengthens Samsung and SK Hynix's bargaining position with Apple and keeps DRAM pricing firm. CXMT separately reported 716% YoY revenue growth, becoming the world's fastest-growing DRAM maker.

bullets.title: Samsung and SK Hynix evaluate Chinese AMEC etching equipment for China fabs
bullets.body: Reuters reports Samsung and SK Hynix began testing AMEC etchers approximately two years ago as a hedge against U.S. sanctions making it difficult to bring equipment into Chinese fabrication plants. The evaluation reflects escalating concerns about supply chain resilience as export control risk intensifies.

bullets.title: Fed's Schmid: AI investment is an inflation driver; current policy not restrictive enough
bullets.body: KC Fed President Schmid (non-voter) became the fifth Fed official since last week's FOMC to signal openness to rate action, explicitly flagging AI investment as a potential inflation driver and stating the Fed 'should not ignore' it. He characterized current monetary policy as not restrictive and said tighter policy is needed to sustainably return inflation to 2%. Markets were briefly pricing a 58% chance of a September hike before the print, though one source suggests the probability is lower.

bullets.title: S&P 500 closes at first record since June; Nasdaq 100 up ~945 bps in four sessions
bullets.body: The S&P 500 and Dow hit all-time highs on Hormuz deal optimism, strong earnings, and falling oil. Goldman's Peter Callahan flagged the Nasdaq-100's 9.38% four-session return as the 6th-best such period in 20 years. $8.3T sits in money market funds at an all-time high, and a $16M SPY call sweep with a 31x V/OI ratio was flagged as highly unusual institutional conviction. Michael Burry publicly bet against the rally, calling for a potential 1987-style crash.

bullets.title: Oil -5.7% to $75.77/bbl on Hormuz deal hopes; Polymarket puts reopen at 32%
bullets.body: WTI crude settled down 5.69% at $75.77/bbl and Brent below $80 on prospects of a U.S.-Iran interim deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz—though Iran denied knowledge of imminent talks and rejected an earlier Omani framework. Polymarket assigns 32% probability to Strait traffic normalization by September 30. Trump said gas prices 'could fall if Hormuz reopens.'

bullets.title: AI datacenter buildout: 15GW+ of new capacity being built without backup generators
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis datacenter team identified 15GW+ of new capacity—including at Microsoft and Meta GPU halls—being constructed without gensets or central UPS. The trend reflects training workload tolerance for downtime via checkpointing, cutting capex and accelerating deployment timelines. ABF substrate makers are being pre-funded for 2029–2030 capacity expansions as AI chip die sizes grow and LTAs prove insufficient.

bullets.title: Telecom stocks (VZ, T) fall 4%+ on SpaceX competitive threat comments
bullets.body: Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile each fell more than 4% on SpaceX earnings call comments about Starlink's ambitions. Musk stated it is 'not out of the question' that Starlink delivers the majority of global internet within 10 years. SpaceX also announced it acquired EchoStar spectrum, adding to competitive pressure on incumbent telcos.

bullets.title: SNDK and WDC report after close Wednesday; SanDisk/SK Hynix announce High Bandwidth Flash standard
bullets.body: SanDisk and Western Digital are scheduled to report Q2 earnings after Wednesday's close. Separately, SK Hynix in collaboration with SanDisk unveiled a new High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) standard designed to address AI inference memory bottlenecks, targeting up to 3TB/s bandwidth. One fintwit account noted a meeting with SanDisk management at Flash Memory Summit on Thursday.
